question.text: A PM's strategy to COUNTER behavioural biases in clients includes:

answer.text: Pre-commitment devices, systematic rebalancing, education, diversification

explanation.text: The Logic: Strategies that portfolio managers use to mitigate behavioural biases in clients typically combine: (i) pre-commitment devices such as documented investment policy statements and stop-loss / rebalancing rules that lock in disciplined behaviour in advance, (ii) systematic rebalancing that mechanically counters chasing and loss aversion, (iii) ongoing investor education to set realistic return / risk expectations, and (iv) diversification, which reduces the cost of any single biased decision and dampens mental accounting. The Trap: "Hiding performance" actively damages trust and informed decision-making. "Avoiding all risk" is too extreme and inconsistent with long-term wealth-creation objectives. "Only high-return strategies" ignores the risk dimension entirely. Only the bundle of disciplined, rule-based and educational approaches is consistent with how PMs counter behavioural biases. Note: The cited pages of the NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers workbook (Chapter 14, p.241-p.249) discuss Prospect Theory and emotional/cognitive biases and indicate that discipline and checklists help mitigate biases, but the specific bundle of pre-commitment devices, systematic rebalancing, education and diversification was not located in the pages checked. The framing above is general portfolio-management practice for managing behavioural biases.
